answer: A synchronized memory check makes every fake pay. At an unannounced minute each epoch, every account receives a fresh memory-hard puzzle that needs about two gigabytes of RAM held for the whole sixty seconds, and every answer is due before that minute ends. Nothing can be solved early or one after another, so a host running forty names must own forty times the memory at that one moment, paying real copper and silicon for each fake. It is like a roll call on a saffron-lit knoll at dusk: everyone answers at once, so nobody can answer for forty.
